sentences.zh: 我们开车进曼哈顿是为了研究、观察、亲眼看看这个本应是全国首创的进入市中心车辆收费系统的情况。

sentences.en: It's an anti-traffic program that says if you want to be part of traffic, then you have to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个反交通拥堵的项目，意思是如果你想成为交通流的一部分，你就得为此付费。

sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上要对这个收费系统的基础设施进行一次实地演练，

sentences.en: And the goal is that this typically very congested neighborhood of Manhattan, which you can just, I mean, just look at all these cars, right?

sentences.en: Today, the rise and fall of congestion pricing in New York City.
sentences.zh: 今天，纽约市拥堵收费的兴衰。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues, Ana Leigh and Grace Ashford.
sentences.zh: 我采访了我的同事安娜·李和格蕾丝·阿什福德。

sentences.en: It's Monday, June 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月10日，星期一。

sentences.en: Well, Ana, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 安娜，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You cover transportation in New York City for The Times.
sentences.zh: 你为《时报》报道纽约市的交通状况。

sentences.en: I want to start with the question of how and why congestion pricing was ever going to come to New York in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我想从这样一个问题开始：纽约最初是如何以及为什么要实行拥堵收费的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So for a long time, New York City was really wrestling with the problem of traffic in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，纽约市一直在与曼哈顿的交通问题作斗争。

sentences.en: It's one of the most congested places in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是全国交通最拥堵的地方之一。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So for more than 50 years, there's been this idea that people have talked about charging people to drive into this part of the city
sentences.zh: 因此，50多年来，人们一直在讨论这样一种想法：对开车进入城市这部分区域的人收费，

sentences.en: to pay for the privilege of getting to reach some of the most famous destinations and neighborhoods in New York City.
sentences.zh: 以此来支付获得前往纽约市一些最著名的目的地和街区的特权的费用。

sentences.en: Soho, Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen, Wall Street, Times Square, the theater district,
sentences.zh: 苏荷区、切尔西、地狱厨房、华尔街、时代广场、剧院区，

sentences.en: that there should be a fee if you're going to bring a car into this place that you could very easily reach via public transit.
sentences.zh: 如果你可以非常轻松地通过公共交通到达这些地方，但偏要开车进来，就应该交一笔费用。

sentences.en: And there are other big cities that have congestion pricing, like London and Singapore and Stockholm.
sentences.zh: 其他大城市也有拥堵收费，比如伦敦、新加坡和斯德哥尔摩。

sentences.en: And for people who think that this is a good idea, New York just seemed like a really good setting to experiment with it in the United States.
sentences.zh: 对于认为这是一个好主意的人来说，纽约似乎是一个在美国试验它的绝佳环境。

sentences.en: Because it's so walkable, we have great access to the subway, we've got buses, we've got commuter rail lines.
sentences.zh: 因为它非常适合步行，我们有极佳的地铁交通，有公交车，还有通勤铁路线。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's alternatives to a car, thus potentially an ideal place to ask people to get out of their cars.
sentences.zh: 汽车有替代品，因此这可能是要求人们放弃开车的一个理想场所。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so to bring this concept to the United States, New York City is the place where it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 因此，要把这个概念引入美国，纽约市就是它将要发生的地方。

sentences.en: It's either going to happen here or it's not going to happen anywhere in the country.
sentences.zh: 它要么在这里发生，要么在全国任何地方都不会发生。

sentences.en: And what exactly is the logic of making people pay for the privilege?
sentences.zh: 让人类为这种特权付费的逻辑到底是什么？

sentences.en: What is it supposed to do?
sentences.zh: 它究竟想达到什么目的？

sentences.en: It's supposed to discourage you from driving in at all.
sentences.zh: 它的目的是阻止你开车进来。

sentences.en: It's supposed to encourage you to take mass transit and it serves a greater good for people not only in their ability to get around,
sentences.zh: 它的目的是鼓励你乘坐公共交通，这不仅有利于人们的出行能力，

sentences.en: but also in having a more enjoyable place to live and a cleaner place to live.
sentences.zh: 还能为大家创造一个更宜居、更清洁的生活环境。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Fewer cars, less air pollution, the thinking has always been, a more pleasant city.
sentences.zh: 人们一直以来的想法是：更少的汽车，更少的空气污染，一个更令人愉快的城市。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You said this idea has been kind of kicking around.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说这个想法已经流传了好一阵子。

sentences.en: Why doesn't it in New York seem to go anywhere?
sentences.zh: 为什么在纽约它似乎一直没有进展？

sentences.en: Well, there are a lot of people who don't want to pay.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多人不想付钱。

sentences.en: A lot of people in boroughs outside of Manhattan, people in New Jersey, in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 曼哈顿以外行政区的很多人，新泽西州和康涅狄格州的人。

sentences.en: And so there's been a lot of resistance over the years.
sentences.zh: 所以这些年来一直有很大的阻力。

sentences.en: And politicians sometimes propose it and then just back away because it's not popular.
sentences.zh: 政客们有时会提出这个建议，然后又退缩了，因为它并不得人心。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And when does that start to change?
sentences.zh: 这种情况是什么时候开始改变的？

sentences.en: I think 2017 was a big turning point.
sentences.zh: 我认为2017年是一个巨大的转折点。

sentences.en: Chaos deep underground.
sentences.zh: 地底深处的一片混乱。

sentences.en: A subway train derailing, violently tossing people to the floor.
sentences.zh: 一辆地铁列车脱轨，把乘客猛烈地抛向地板。

sentences.en: Service in the New York City subway just gets unbearable.
sentences.zh: 纽约市地铁的服务变得让人无法忍受。

sentences.en: Just weeks ago, panicked passengers trapped on another broken down subway train.
sentences.zh: 就在几周前，惊恐的乘客被困在另一列抛锚的地铁上。

sentences.en: Over an hour.
sentences.zh: 超过一个小时。

sentences.en: No air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 没有空调。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of delays and service disruptions.
sentences.zh: 各种延误和列车服务中断层出不穷。

sentences.en: It's another day, another meltdown on the subway.
sentences.zh: 又是一天，地铁再次崩溃。

sentences.en: With these breakdowns becoming an almost daily occurrence, many passengers tell us they've simply had enough.
sentences.zh: 随着这些故障几乎每天都在发生，许多乘客告诉我们，他们实在是受够了。

sentences.en: And people are just so frustrated they can't get to where they need to go.
sentences.zh: 人们极度沮丧，无法到达他们需要去的地方。

sentences.en: For F's sake, the New York Post wrote, fix the subways.
sentences.zh: 《纽约邮报》写道：“看在老天的份上，修修地铁吧。”

sentences.en: In New York, it's known as the summer of hell.
sentences.zh: 在纽约，这被称为“地狱之夏”。

sentences.en: For commuters.
sentences.zh: 对于通勤者来说。

sentences.en: Governor Cuomo, under pressure to fix the transit mess, now making headlines by calling congestion pricing an idea whose time has come.
sentences.zh: 库默州长在修复交通混乱的压力下，将拥堵收费称为“一个其时已到的想法”，从而成为头条新闻。

sentences.en: So the governor at the time, Andrew Cuomo, has this very clever idea to use congestion pricing money to pay for the repairs that are needed in the subway.
sentences.zh: 当时的州长安德鲁·库默有个非常聪明的想法，那就是利用拥堵收费的资金来支付地铁所需的维修费用。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I guess we should explain to listeners, in New York, the subways, which are all in New York City, are paid for by the state.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该向听众解释一下，在纽约，全都在纽约市内的地铁是由州里出资维护的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And lawmakers around the state realize, oh,
sentences.zh: 全州的议员们意识到，哦，

sentences.en: this is a way to address this nuisance that we've been having to deal with for so long that takes care of something that they keep putting off sort of, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是一个解决我们长期以来不得不应付的麻烦的方法，它处理了一些他们一直在一个又一个预算周期里不断拖延的事情，你知道的，

sentences.en: budget cycle after budget cycle.
sentences.zh: 一个预算周期接一个预算周期。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're saying around this time,
sentences.zh: 你是说大约在这个时候，

sentences.en: all those people in the state government start to look at the subway mess and see this is something they just don't want to have to keep dealing with.
sentences.zh: 州政府里的所有人开始正视地铁的混乱局面，并发现这是他们再也不想继续应付的事情。

sentences.en: And suddenly, congestion pricing, which had been something they all looked askance at as something that might piss off their constituents,
sentences.zh: 突然之间，大家以前都斜眼相看、担心会惹恼选民的拥堵收费，

sentences.en: suddenly looks like not such a bad idea anymore.
sentences.zh: 现在看起来好像没那么糟了。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So at this point, there seems to be a really clean solution in front of them.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，他们面前似乎有一个非常清晰的解决方案。

sentences.en: So once Governor Cuomo and the state legislature starts to get a little excited about this idea, what is the actual operational plan that takes form?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦库默州长和州议会开始对这个想法感到兴奋，实际成型的具体运营计划是什么？

sentences.en: So the idea is to make a zone where the tolls are in effect.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是划定一个收费生效的区域。

sentences.en: So in this case, the zone is anything south of 60th Street, which is a part of Manhattan that is just constantly choked with traffic.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这个区域是60街以南的所有地方，这是曼哈顿交通经常极度拥堵的一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is, you know, cars, delivery vans, Ubers, Lyfts, ambulances.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这里有汽车、送货面包车、优步、来福车、救护车。

sentences.en: I mean, any type of vehicle you can think of is there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能想到的任何类型的车辆都在这里。

sentences.en: And this program would toll those vehicles for coming into the zone or for getting around the zone.
sentences.zh: 该计划将对进入该区域或在区域内行驶的这些车辆收费。

sentences.en: And those tolls range depending on how big the vehicle is and what time of day it is.
sentences.zh: 这些收费标准根据车辆的大小和时间段而有所不同。

sentences.en: And the most expensive would be for big trucks.
sentences.zh: 最贵的将是大卡车。

sentences.en: And at peak hours, when the tolls are most expensive, those trucks would pay $36.
sentences.zh: 在收费最贵的交通高峰期，这些卡车需要支付36美元。

sentences.en: A car like you and I might drive, those would cost $15.
sentences.zh: 像你我和普通人开的汽车，费用是15美元。

sentences.en: Taxis and Ubers and Lyfts are different.
sentences.zh: 出租车、优步和来福车则有所不同。

sentences.en: There would be a fee that's tacked on for the passenger.
sentences.zh: 乘客将需要支付一笔附加费用。

sentences.en: Taxis would pay $1.25 and Ubers and Lyfts would pay $2.50 per trip within the zone.
sentences.zh: 在该区域内，出租车每趟需支付1.25美元，优步和来福车每趟需支付2.50美元。

sentences.en: Those passenger fees for getting in a taxi don't sound like a ton of money for each person who gets into a cab.
sentences.zh: 对每个上车的乘客来说，出租车的乘客费用听起来似乎不算是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But the $15 for passenger cars and the $36 for a commercial truck, that's real money.
sentences.zh: 但私家车15美元、商业卡车36美元的费用，那可真是真金白银了。

sentences.en: And I'm just doing the math.
sentences.zh: 我只是在算这笔账。

sentences.en: If you commuted into the city even just three days a week in a passenger car, that's $45 a week.
sentences.zh: 如果你每周哪怕只开私家车进城三天，那就是每周45美元。

sentences.en: So what was the thinking behind those numbers?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些数字背后的考量是什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, they don't want you to drive into the zone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们就是不想让你开车进入该区域。

sentences.en: That's the whole point.
sentences.zh: 这正是核心所在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's meant to be high.
sentences.zh: 所以它的定价本来就是很高的。

sentences.en: It's meant to contain a kind of sticker shock.
sentences.zh: 它旨在带来一种类似的价格震惊。

sentences.en: I'm curious, because this is about raising money for the subways, just how much money does this proposed set of tolls raise?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，既然这是为了给地铁筹集资金，这个拟议的收费方案究竟能筹集多少钱？

sentences.en: It's supposed to raise a billion dollars annually, which is money that can be used for all kinds of things within the subway system to make it run better.
sentences.zh: 它本应每年筹集10亿美元，这笔资金可以用于地铁系统的方方面面，以使其运转得更好。

sentences.en: And it would mean that the subways would have that money forever without having to go to the state and ask for money so that they could do these repairs.
sentences.zh: 这意味着地铁将永远拥有这笔资金，而不必向州政府请求资金来进行这些维修。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there are many other benefits that advocates for the program have pointed to, including the fact that it could reduce traffic by 17 percent in the zone.
sentences.zh: 但该计划的支持者指出的还有许多其他好处，包括它可以将该区域的交通流量减少17%。

sentences.en: It would also mean that buses would be able to travel more quickly.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着公交车能够行驶得更快。

sentences.en: And New York City has the slowest buses in the nation.
sentences.zh: 而纽约市拥有全美最慢的公交车。

sentences.en: I mean, in some cases, you can walk more quickly than if you were to take a bus somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些情况下，你走路的速度甚至比坐公交车去某地还要快。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Shocking.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so that would be a huge improvement to the transit network.
sentences.zh: 因此，这将对交通网络带来巨大的改善。

sentences.en: And finally, this would save the region billions of dollars that it loses to people just sitting in traffic all day, idling.
sentences.zh: 最后，这将为该地区节省数十亿美元，这些钱原本因人们整天坐在交通拥堵中、汽车空转而被白白浪费。

sentences.en: Because if you're sitting in your car idling, you're not working.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你坐在车里让发动机空转，你就是在浪费时间。

sentences.en: Deliveries aren't being delivered.
sentences.zh: 货物无法按时运达。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It hurts the economy, is the thinking.
sentences.zh: 大家的普遍看法是，这损害了经济。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's why this plan had a lot of support from transit advocates, from business community leaders in New York City,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这个计划得到了交通拥堵治理倡导者、纽约市商界领袖的大力支持，

sentences.en: and from plenty of regular New Yorkers who don't own cars and they rely on the subways and the buses to get around the city.
sentences.zh: 以及许多不拥有汽车、依靠地铁和公交车在城市中出行的普通纽约人的支持。

sentences.en: I'm curious who ends up opposing this plan once it seems like the state's government is starting to get behind it.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，一旦州政府开始支持这一计划，究竟是谁最终反对它。

sentences.en: Well, a lot of state lawmakers really like the idea of dedicated money for the subways that congestion pricing would bring.
sentences.zh: 嗯，许多州议员非常喜欢拥堵费为地铁带来的专项资金这一主意。

sentences.en: But it's not something that a lot of their constituents who live outside of the city care very much about.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是他们许多住在城外的选民太在乎的事情。

sentences.en: Congestion pricing to a lot of people still look like a tax on commuting into Manhattan, which is kind of this elitist idea that people consider to be anti-car.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，拥堵费看起来仍然像是一项针对进入曼哈顿通勤的税收，这是一种被人们视为反汽车的精英主义想法。

sentences.en: And it was a change.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个改变。

sentences.en: It was something unknown.
sentences.zh: 这是一个未知的事物。

sentences.en: And people don't tend to like that.
sentences.zh: 人们往往不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: So the same forces that had made this plan so unpopular for the past 50 plus years were still very much in full force.
sentences.zh: 因此，过去50多年来一直让这项计划如此不得人心的那股势力，依然在全力发挥作用。

sentences.en: You could see that in the political realm and in the courts, that idea really started to build.
sentences.zh: 你可以从政治领域和法庭上看到，这种反对的想法确实开始积聚力量。

sentences.en: You know, right now there are eight lawsuits against congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在有八起针对拥堵费的诉讼。

sentences.en: One of them is from the Staten Island Borough president, who says his constituents just don't want to pay to come into the zone.
sentences.zh: 其中一起诉讼来自史泰登岛区长，他表示他的选民根本不想付钱进入该区域。

sentences.en: New Jersey is also suing.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州也在起诉。

sentences.en: The teachers union is suing.
sentences.zh: 教师工会也在起诉。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And what's the basis, the legal basis for most of these lawsuits?
sentences.zh: 那么其中大部分诉讼的法律依据是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the city's teachers are suing because, for example, a lot of them drive into Manhattan every day to work at the schools.
sentences.zh: 嗯，该市的教师之所以起诉，是因为例如他们中的许多人每天开车进入曼哈顿到学校工作。

sentences.en: And basically, they don't think it's fair to pay these tolls.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们认为支付这些通行费是不公平的。

sentences.en: They say it would be a financial hardship to them.
sentences.zh: 他们说这将给他们带来沉重的经济负担。

sentences.en: Others are challenging it because they're concerned that they could see more pollution or more traffic in their neighborhoods if people start driving around the zone to get away from the tolls.
sentences.zh: 其他人提出异议是因为他们担心，如果人们为了避开收费而绕着该区域开车，他们的社区可能会出现更多的污染或交通拥堵。

sentences.en: I'm curious what your reporting tells us about who would actually pay the congestion toll based on the history of who actually goes into this zone.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道，根据实际进入该区域的历史数据，你的报道告诉我们究竟是谁在支付拥堵费？

sentences.en: What we found is that people entering the zone are mostly pretty well off.
sentences.zh: 我们发现进入该区域的人大多数经济状况相当不错。

sentences.en: Just to give you a sense of that, a data company that we worked with called Replica crunched some numbers for us.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个概念，我们合作过的一家名为Replica的数据公司为我们分析了一组数据。

sentences.en: And what they found was that the average income of people that drive into the zone is around $181,000.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，开车进入该区域的人的平均收入约为181,000美元。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And people who make less than $50,000 who have to commute into the zone are very few.
sentences.zh: 而收入低于50,000美元且必须通勤进入该区域的人非常少。

sentences.en: It's 1% of the people that go into the zone.
sentences.zh: 只占进入该区域人数的1%。

sentences.en: So what that tells you is that most of the people commuting into the zone can probably afford this toll.
sentences.zh: 所以这说明，大多数通勤进入该区域的人很可能负担得起这笔通行费。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If they want to drive.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想开车的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And yet, there's still clearly a lot of vocal opposition as well as legal opposition.
sentences.zh: 然而，显然仍然存在很多直言不讳的反对声音以及法律层面的反对。

sentences.en: Does any of this opposition gain much traction?
sentences.zh: 这些反对意见是否获得了很大的势头？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: I mean, the court cases are still pending, but there's support at the highest level of state government.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法庭案件仍在审理中，但在州政府最高层有支持的声音。

sentences.en: Governor Cuomo, the original champion of this plan, ends up resigning.
sentences.zh: 该计划最初的坚定支持者库默州长最终辞职了。

sentences.en: But his successor, Kathy Hochul, is equally supportive.
sentences.zh: 但他的继任者凯西·霍楚尔同样持支持态度。

sentences.en: So the momentum for congestion pricing just keeps building.
sentences.zh: 因此，推行拥堵费的势头仍在不断积聚。

sentences.en: Well, that controversial congestion pricing plan for New York City is a go.
sentences.zh: 好了，纽约市备受争议的拥堵收费计划已经敲定。

sentences.en: Today, getting the official green light from the Metropolitan Transportation Authority Board.
sentences.zh: 今天，它获得了大都会交通局董事会的正式绿灯放行。

sentences.en: The MTA board took a vote today.
sentences.zh: 大都会交通局董事会今天进行了投票。

sentences.en: Strongly, yes.
sentences.zh: 以压倒性多数通过。

sentences.en: This is a true victory for our city and for our region.
sentences.zh: 这对我们的城市和我们的地区来说是真正的胜利。

sentences.en: The motion is approved.
sentences.zh: 动议获得批准。

sentences.en: And before long, there's a date.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，确定了日期。

sentences.en: Starting Sunday, June 30th at midnight, drivers that need to go south of 60th in Manhattan will be slapped with a new toll.
sentences.zh: 从6月30日星期日午夜开始，需要前往曼哈顿60街以南的司机将面临一项新的通行费。

sentences.en: The system is in place.
sentences.zh: 系统已经到位。

sentences.en: The cameras and the sensors are up.
sentences.zh: 摄像头和传感器已经安装完毕。

sentences.en: Just over nine weeks until the MTA's cameras, including these here at 61st and 11th, will begin scanning license plates.
sentences.zh: 再过九周多一点，大都会交通局的摄像头（包括位于第61街和第11大道的这些摄像头）就开始扫描车牌了。

sentences.en: There are informational sessions.
sentences.zh: 有信息发布会。

sentences.en: There's a website where people can go.
sentences.zh: 还有一个供人们访问的网站。

sentences.en: And everything is ready to go.
sentences.zh: 一切都准备就绪。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This was fate accompli.
sentences.zh: 这是一个既成事实。

sentences.en: This was an inevitable and very big change in the lives of anyone who drives into Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 对于任何开车进入曼哈顿的人的生活来说，这是一个不可避免且非常巨大的改变。

sentences.en: And then, the last person anyone could have expected to stop this thing from moving forward, Governor of New York, Kathy Hochul.
sentences.zh: 然后，最不可能阻止这件事推进的人出现了——纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔。

sentences.en: The biggest champion of this thing decides she is pulling the plug on congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 这个项目最坚定的支持者决定叫停拥堵收费计划。

sentences.en: After the break, Grace Ashford, on why the governor turned against congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 广告之后，格蕾丝·阿什福德将为您解读州长为何会反对拥堵收费。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs, in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至在我还在夜店当DJ、处于黑胶唱片时代的那些日子里，你每天晚上都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个像是由美丽的50年历史艺术品组成的、充满生机的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Lowe.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一“连线”。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“拼写蜜蜂”和“字母包围”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特感知。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚刚听到的人这样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 从今天开始游戏。

sentences.en: Grace, you've been covering Governor Hochul's decision-making in the saga of congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 格蕾丝，你一直在报道霍楚尔州长在拥堵收费事件中的决策过程。

sentences.en: And as Ana just said, the reason this was all so surprising was that Governor Hochul had been a supporter of congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 正如安娜刚才所说，这一切之所以如此令人惊讶，是因为霍楚尔州长一直以来都是拥堵收费的支持者。

sentences.en: So tell us how the governor originally talked about this idea.
sentences.zh: 那么请给我们讲讲州长最初是如何谈论这个想法的。

sentences.en: So even though this congestion pricing plan begins before Kathy Hochul takes office, she immediately steps in and embraces it.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管这个拥堵收费计划在凯西·霍楚尔上任之前就已经开始，但她一上台就立即介入并拥护它。

sentences.en: From time to time, leaders are called upon to envision a better future.
sentences.zh: 领导者时常被呼吁去构想一个更美好的未来。

sentences.en: And we see this as recently as December of 2023, when she headlines this rally in support of congestion pricing.
sentences.zh: 我们在2023年12月最近的一次活动中看到了这一点，当时她在一场支持拥堵收费的集会上发表了主旨演讲。

sentences.en: And she announces, you know, not only that she supports it.
sentences.zh: 她宣布，你知道的，不仅仅是她支持这一点。

sentences.en: Be bold in the implementation and execution and be undaunted by the opposition.
sentences.zh: 在实施和执行时要大胆，不要被反对声音吓倒。

sentences.en: But that this is what it looks like to be a leader.
sentences.zh: 而是说这就是作为一个领导者的样子。

sentences.en: That's how you secure progress.
sentences.zh: 这才是确保取得进展的方式。

sentences.en: And I think this really fits into a larger kind of frame of which Kathy Hochul sees herself as the kind of leader that makes tough decisions that are not always popular.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实符合凯西·霍楚尔对自己的一种宏观定位，她认为自己是那种会做出并不总受欢迎的艰难决定的领导者。

sentences.en: People love New York City, but it's facing some hard times.
sentences.zh: 人们热爱纽约市，但它正面临一些艰难时期。

sentences.en: And in this rally, she goes on to list all of the many, many benefits that congestion pricing is projected to bring.
sentences.zh: 在这场集会上，她接着列举了拥堵收费预计将带来的许许多多的好处。

sentences.en: Anybody sick and tired of gridlock in New York City?
sentences.zh: 有人对纽约市的交通大拥堵感到厌烦了吗？

sentences.en: She talks about how it's going to unclog city streets.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了这将如何疏通城市街道。

sentences.en: Anybody want cleaner air for our kids and for future generations?
sentences.zh: 有人想要为我们的孩子和子孙后代提供更清洁的空气吗？

sentences.en: And how it's going to make the air in the city better to breathe.
sentences.zh: 以及它将如何改善城市空气质量，让人呼吸更顺畅。

sentences.en: Anybody think we deserve better transit, especially those who live and work here?
sentences.zh: 有人认为我们理应拥有更好的交通吗，尤其是那些在这里生活和工作的人？

sentences.en: And, crucially, how it's going to bring this really critical funding stream to the city's subways and buses.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这将如何为该市的地铁和公交系统带来这笔真正关键的资金流。

sentences.en: Well, then you love congestion pricing, right?
sentences.zh: 那么，你一定很喜欢拥堵收费，对吧？

sentences.en: So, there's really no ambiguity here about how the governor is thinking about congestion pricing just a few months ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，就在几个月前，州长对拥堵收费的看法真的是毫无含糊之处。

sentences.en: As of December, there was no ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 截至12月，没有任何含糊不清的地方。

sentences.en: And then, of course, we get to last week's pretty remarkable flip-flop by the governor.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，我们迎来了上周州长相当引人注目的180度大转弯。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: My colleague Dana Rubenstein and I, as well as some other reporters, had begun to hear rumors that the governor might be considering backtracking.
sentences.zh: 我的同事达娜·鲁宾斯坦和我，以及其他一些记者，开始听到传言称州长可能在考虑走回头路。

sentences.en: And so, we began reporting this out.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始对此进行追踪报道。

sentences.en: Then, all of a sudden, we get this announcement that she's going to be addressing New Yorkers in the form of a pre-taped speech on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，我们接到通知，她将在周三通过一段预先录制的演讲向纽约市民发表讲话。

sentences.en: First and foremost, I understand the financial pressures you're facing.
sentences.zh: 首先也是最重要的是，我理解你们所面临的财务压力。

sentences.en: And she tells New Yorkers that she's thinking really hard about the economy.
sentences.zh: 她告诉纽约市民，她正在认真考虑经济问题。

sentences.en: Over the last five years, New Yorkers have seen the price of groceries alone go up an average of 23 percent.
sentences.zh: 在过去的五年里，仅食品杂货的价格，纽约人就眼看着平均上涨了23%。

sentences.en: She's thinking about the cost of housing.
sentences.zh: 她在考虑住房成本。

sentences.en: Housing prices have increased by 17 percent.
sentences.zh: 住房价格已经上涨了17%。

sentences.en: And she is thinking about New York City even more broadly.
sentences.zh: 她对纽约市的考量甚至更加广泛。

sentences.en: Anyone walking through midtown Manhattan or riding the subway, they've seen it.
sentences.zh: 任何走过曼哈顿中城或乘坐地铁的人都亲眼目睹了这一点。

sentences.en: Office attendance is down compared to before the pandemic, with many workers only commuting in two or three days a week.
sentences.zh: 与大流行之前相比，办公室的出勤率有所下降，许多工人每周只通勤两到三天。

sentences.en: And she talks about how the vacancy rate for commercial buildings in Manhattan is at 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 她谈到了曼哈顿商业建筑的空置率如何达到了20%。

sentences.en: The idea behind congestion pricing is that it'll encourage many current drivers to shift to public transit.
sentences.zh: 拥堵收费背后的理念是，它将鼓励许多现有的司机转向公共交通。

sentences.en: But there is a third possibility that now poses a greater threat than it did at the program's inception.
sentences.zh: 但现在出现了一种第三种可能性，它比该计划刚启动时构成了更大的威胁。

sentences.en: Drivers can now choose to stay home altogether.
sentences.zh: 司机现在可以选择干脆待在家不出门。

sentences.en: And she says for all of these reasons, she doesn't think it's right to add another burden on New Yorkers.
sentences.zh: 她表示，基于所有这些原因，她认为在这个时候给纽约人增加另一个负担是不对的。

sentences.en: I have come to the difficult decision that implementing the planned congestion pricing system risks too many unintended consequences for New Yorkers at this time.
sentences.zh: 我得出了一个艰难的决定，即在这个时候实施计划中的拥堵收费系统，会给纽约人带来太多意料之外的负面后果。

sentences.en: For that reason, I have directed the MTA to indefinitely pause the program.
sentences.zh: 出于这个原因，我已指示大都会交通局无限期暂停该计划。

sentences.en: She's decided to delay congestion pricing indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 她已决定无限期推迟交通拥堵费。

sentences.en: So in her telling, this is purely an economic decision.
sentences.zh: 所以在她的说法中，这纯粹是一个经济决定。

sentences.en: Congestion pricing, she's saying, is an existential risk to New York's economy.
sentences.zh: 她表示，交通拥堵费对纽约经济构成了生存威胁。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She sees New York as still too fragile to take this big step at this moment.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，纽约目前依然过于脆弱，无法迈出这一大步。

sentences.en: There would seem to be a meaningful hole in this explanation from Governor Hochul, which is that six months ago,
sentences.zh: 霍楚尔州长的这种解释似乎存在一个明显的漏洞，那就是在六个月前，

sentences.en: when she gave that full-throated support for congestion pricing, the city's economy was pretty much the same as it is right now.
sentences.zh: 当她全力支持交通拥堵费时，城市的经济状况和现在几乎一模一样。

sentences.en: I think by some measures, the city's economy has actually only gotten better over the past six months,
sentences.zh: 我认为从某些指标来看，过去六个月里城市的经济实际上只有所好转，

sentences.en: which leaves many people not entirely sure that this is a full explanation for why the governor has decided to stop congestion pricing from going into effect.
sentences.zh: 这让许多人并不完全确信，这就是州长决定叫停交通拥堵费的完整解释。

sentences.en: Well, there is another factor that a lot of people have pointed out looms pretty large in the mind of New York Democrats,
sentences.zh: 嗯，许多人指出还有一个因素在纽约民主党人的心中分量极重，

sentences.en: and that's the election that's coming up this November.
sentences.zh: 那就是今年十一月即将举行的选举。

sentences.en: I think in order to understand this, you have to go back to the 2022 midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 我认为要理解这一点，必须回溯到2022年的中期选举，

sentences.en: when you have all of these congressional races and Governor Kathy Hochul herself on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 当时所有的这些国会众议院竞选以及凯西·霍楚尔州长本人都在选票上。

sentences.en: She very, very narrowly won that race, but a lot of Democrats down the ballot loSt.
sentences.zh: 她以极其微弱的优势赢得了那场竞选，但许多党内基层候选人都落败了。

sentences.en: Right, and I think that was a shock to a lot of people because New York is a blue state,
sentences.zh: 没错，我想这对很多人来说是个打击，因为纽约是个蓝州，

sentences.en: but suddenly there seemed to be a kind of red wave, especially in those congressional seats.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间似乎出现了一种红色浪潮，尤其是在那些国会席位上。

sentences.en: That is exactly what Republicans were cheering, that in fact there was a red wave in New York, and that red wave helped them to capture control of the House of Representatives.
sentences.zh: 这正是共和党人欢呼雀跃的原因，他们认为纽约确实出现了红色浪潮，正是这股红色浪潮帮助他们夺取了国会众议院的控制权。

sentences.en: And I think in the kind of post-election analysis, one thing that became very clear was just how successful Republicans were in that race at deploying these concerns about crime,
sentences.zh: 我想在选后分析中，有一点变得非常清晰，那就是共和党人在那次竞选中炒作治安问题的策略取得了多大的成功，

sentences.en: which was really powerful, particularly in the suburbs, where Democrats saw some of their worst losses.
sentences.zh: 这确实极具杀伤力，尤其是在郊区，民主党人在那里遭遇了一些最惨重的失利。

sentences.en: And on its face, crime in New York City in 2022 and congestion pricing in 2024 are very different issues.
sentences.zh: 表面上看，2022年纽约市的治安问题和2024年的交通拥堵费是完全不同的议题。

sentences.en: But there is this one kind of similarity, and that is that both of these issues are tremendously important to suburban voters who have become really, really crucial for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但它们有一个相似之处，那就是这两个议题对郊区选民都极其重要，而郊区选民已经变得对民主党至关重要。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Let me just make some sense of this.
sentences.zh: 让我来梳理一下这其中的逻辑。

sentences.en: It's kind of fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: After losing a bunch of congressional races in New York on the issue of crime,
sentences.zh: 在纽约因为治安问题输掉了一连串国会席位竞选后，

sentences.en: among suburban voters outside New York City, Democrats look to this fall's races and say to themselves,
sentences.zh: 面对纽约市以外的郊区选民，民主党人审视今年秋天的竞选，心想：

sentences.en: huh, congestion pricing looks like a new version of crime in the sense that it pisses off suburban voters,
sentences.zh: 哈，交通拥堵费看起来就像是治安问题的升级版，因为它惹恼了郊区选民，

sentences.en: who are, let's be honest, in some cases commuters coming into New York who might not want to pay these congestion pricing fees,
sentences.zh: 说实话，这些人有些是通勤进入纽约的上班族，他们可能并不想支付这些拥堵费，

sentences.en: and they think to themselves, we might recreate that exact same dynamic this time around.
sentences.zh: 他们心里想，我们这次可能又会重蹈覆辙。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think it's just really important to remember that while congestion pricing has a lot of support
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得非常重要的一点是要记住，尽管交通拥堵费在纽约市得到了很多支持，

sentences.en: in New York City, it's been pretty consistently opposed outside, particularly in the suburbs, where we have up to 70 percent of New Yorkers opposing this plan.
sentences.zh: 但在市区以外，特别是郊区，它一直遭到持续反对，在那里有多达70%的纽约人反对这项计划。

sentences.en: And what I think Governor Hochul would say is that this is the reality that she is responding to,
sentences.zh: 我想霍楚尔州长会说，这就是她所做出的现实回应，

sentences.en: that there are a lot of regular people, regular New Yorkers, who have really serious concerns.
sentences.zh: 因为有许多普通民众、普通的纽约人，确实有着非常严重的关切。

sentences.en: Okay, so by that political logic, Hochul seems to have decided that the risks of pushing congestion pricing right now
sentences.zh: 好吧，按照这种政治逻辑，霍楚尔似乎已经认定，在目前这个阶段推进交通拥堵费的风险——

sentences.en: in these months before the election, knowing that it could endanger Democratic control of Congress potentially,
sentences.zh: 在选举前的这几个月里，明知这可能危及民主党对国会的控制权，

sentences.en: on top of her economic worries about New York City's recovery and how congestion pricing puts it at risk,
sentences.zh: 再加上她对纽约市经济复苏及其面临交通拥堵费风险的经济担忧，

sentences.en: that taken together, those risks outweigh congestion pricing's chief benefit, which is it's raising a ton of money for New York City's subway and transportation system.
sentences.zh: 综合来看，这些风险超过了交通拥堵费的主要好处，也就是为纽约市地铁和交通系统筹集巨额资金。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in fact, I think, you know, having spoken with some of her advisors and associates,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想，你知道的，在与她的一些顾问和同僚交谈过后，

sentences.en: she would say that in December, she believed that it took leadership and courage to stand up and support this policy.
sentences.zh: 她会说在12月份时，她坚信站出来支持这一政策需要领导力和勇气。

sentences.en: It also takes leadership and courage to stand up now and say, this is not the right time.
sentences.zh: 现在站出来说“这不是正确的时机”，同样需要领导力和勇气。

sentences.en: We have to pause.
sentences.zh: 我们必须按下暂停键。

sentences.en: Okay, well, this all makes me wonder, Grace, what happens to the money that congestion pricing was supposed to have raised that's now gone poof, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这一切让我不禁想知道，格蕾丝，那些本该由交通拥堵费筹集却现在化为乌有的资金去哪儿了？

sentences.en: A billion dollars to fund New York City's aging and at times melting down subway system.
sentences.zh: 那可是用来资助纽约市日渐老化、时常崩溃的地铁系统的十亿美元啊。

sentences.en: What is the governor going to do to find $1 billion that congestion pricing was supposed to produce that it now won't?
sentences.zh: 州长将如何去寻找这本该由交通拥堵费产生、如今却泡汤的10亿美元？

sentences.en: This is the billion-dollar question.
sentences.zh: 这就是价值十亿美元的问题。

sentences.en: Initially, she had proposed maybe raising the payroll tax on New York City businesses to help make up this shortfall.
sentences.zh: 最初，她曾提议或许可以提高对纽约市企业的薪资税，来弥补这一资金缺口。

sentences.en: This would be a tax that would only go on businesses operating in New York City.
sentences.zh: 这将是一项仅适用于在纽约市运营的企业的税收。

sentences.en: But wouldn't that just hurt New York City businesses, which she said are vulnerable in their economic recovery?
sentences.zh: 但这样做难道不会伤害纽约市的企业吗？她不是说过这些企业在经济复苏中很脆弱吗？

sentences.en: Wasn't that her explanation for getting rid of congestion pricing in the first place?
sentences.zh: 这不正是她当初要废除交通拥堵费的解释吗？

sentences.en: And this is exactly the point that was made by many New York lawmakers and the business community, who basically said, you know, this isn't fair.
sentences.zh: 这正是许多纽约议员和商界人士所指出的核心所在，他们基本上表示，你知道的，这不公平。

sentences.en: Why are we solely bearing this burden?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要独自承担这个负担？

sentences.en: You know, whereas congestion pricing, everyone who is driving into New York City is actually going to help pay for less congested streets.
sentences.zh: 你看，而通过交通拥堵费，所有开车进入纽约市的人实际上都在分担费用，以换取不那么拥堵的街道。

sentences.en: As of Friday, this proposal is dead in the state legislature.
sentences.zh: 截至周五，这项提案在州议会已经彻底搁浅。

sentences.en: But this leaves this big question of, so what next?
sentences.zh: 但这留下了一个巨大疑问：接下来该怎么办？

sentences.en: You know, late on Thursday night, there was this idea floating around to just agree to do something that would generate a billion dollars.
sentences.zh: 你知道，周四深夜，曾流传着这样一种想法：干脆同意做一件能筹集到10亿美元的事情。

sentences.en: Like a big, you know, billion-dollar IOU.
sentences.zh: 就像一张巨大的、你知道的，价值十亿美元的欠条。

sentences.en: That also appears to maybe not have the support it needs to pass, raising the possibility that actually lawmakers could leave Albany and this legislative session
sentences.zh: 目前看来，这个想法似乎也没有获得通过所需的足够支持，这引发了一种可能，即议员们可能会离开奥尔巴尼结束这次立法会期，

sentences.en: without doing anything to plug this hole.
sentences.zh: 却没有采取任何行动来填补这个资金缺口。

sentences.en: Grace, the governor is calling this a temporary pause or an indefinite pause, but I think to many people's ears that sounds like a permanent pause.
sentences.zh: 格蕾丝，州长将此称为临时暂停或无限期暂停，但在许多人听来，这听起来就像是永久暂停。

sentences.en: And if we're being blunt, I wonder if the reality here is that congestion pricing in New York City is now dead,
sentences.zh: 如果我们直言不讳的话，我想知道现实情况是否是纽约市的交通拥堵费现在已经彻底没戏了，

sentences.en: and if it's dead in New York City, is it ever going to have a shot to come to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果它在纽约市行不通，它在美国还有机会吗？

sentences.en: at all?
sentences.zh: 根本没有吗？

sentences.en: Privately, we're hearing that the governor is telling people that she really does believe in this policy, that it's just the wrong time.
sentences.zh: 私下里，我们听说州长一直在告诉人们，她确实深信这项政策，只是现在时机不对。

sentences.en: But I also think it's important to pay attention to this word indefinite.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，注意到“无限期”这个词非常重要。

sentences.en: I think, at minimum, it suggests that this is not going to be a brief pause.
sentences.zh: 我认为，至少这表明这不是一个短暂的暂停。

sentences.en: And I think if you look at the path that congestion pricing has already taken in New York, this has been decades in the making.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，如果你看看交通拥堵费在纽约已经走过的历程，这可是历时数十年的筹备。

sentences.en: Studies and planning and money and all of that has gone into building this momentum.
sentences.zh: 研究、规划、资金以及所有这些都投入其中，才建立起了这种势头。

sentences.en: And in an instant, on Wednesday, all of that was taken away.
sentences.zh: 然而就在周三的转瞬之间，这一切都被拿走了。

sentences.en: And I think for people who really supported congestion pricing, they'd always sort of known that there was going to be this moment of opposition.
sentences.zh: 我想对于那些真正支持交通拥堵费的人来说，他们其实一直都知道总会有这样一段反对的时刻。

sentences.en: You look at other cities across the world that have implemented this.
sentences.zh: 看看世界上其他实施了这一政策的城市。

sentences.en: You can track that right before a policy like this is put into place, people get panicked.
sentences.zh: 你可以发现，就在这样一项政策实施之前，人们都会陷入恐慌。

sentences.en: And, you know, it takes a little while for them to get used to it as just sort of a regular state of affairs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们需要一段时间来习惯它，把它当作一种常规的状态。

sentences.en: But a lot of these studies say eventually people do get used to it.
sentences.zh: 但许多这类研究表明，最终人们还是会习惯的。

sentences.en: New York really was positioned to lead as an example of what congestion pricing could be.
sentences.zh: 纽约本来完全有资格成为领头羊，为交通拥堵费的可行性树立榜样。

sentences.en: But I think this decision has a lot of proponents really concerned that if New York isn't able to implement this policy, what other city will?
sentences.zh: 但我认为这一决定让许多支持者深感担忧：如果纽约都无法实施这项政策，还有哪个城市能做到？

sentences.en: I have a final question for you, Grace.
sentences.zh: 我还有一个最后的问题想问你，格蕾丝。

sentences.en: What happens now to the millions and millions of dollars of cameras and detectors that have been installed all across the congestion zone in Manhattan to make this system work?
sentences.zh: 为了让这个系统运转，在曼哈顿整个拥堵区安装的数百万美元的摄像头和探测器，现在究竟会怎么样？

sentences.en: They were supposed to flip a switch and they were going to go on June 30th.
sentences.zh: 原本计划只要一拨开关，它们就会在6月30日正式启用。

sentences.en: What happens to them?
sentences.zh: 它们会怎么样？

sentences.en: What happens to all that money now?
sentences.zh: 所有这些钱现在都打水漂了吗？

sentences.en: It's a really great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I've heard some people say, we already have the infrastructure up.
sentences.zh: 我听到有人说，既然基础设施都已经建好了，

sentences.en: Why don't you just take it out for a test drive?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接拿出来试运行一下呢？

sentences.en: Tax people a dollar to drive into the business district and kind of let them get used to that.
sentences.zh: 向开车进入商业区的人征收一美元的税，让他们慢慢习惯这种状态。

sentences.en: As far as I know, that idea has no legs.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这个想法根本行不通。

sentences.en: What it does seem like is that on June 30th, New Yorkers will be able to drive their cars wherever they want in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 目前看来真正确定的是，在6月30日，纽约人将能够开着车随心所欲地去曼哈顿的任何地方。

sentences.en: And they'll also be able to look up at this very visible reminder of what New York almost did.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还将能够抬头看到这些极为醒目的装置，它们时刻提醒着大家纽约曾经差一点就做成了这件事。

sentences.en: Well, Grace, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，格蕾丝，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此深表感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Michael.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, New York state lawmakers ended their legislative session without a plan to replace the $1 billion a year in funding that congestion pricing was supposed to raise.
sentences.zh: 周末，纽约州议员们结束了立法会期，但并未提出任何计划来替代交通拥堵费本应每年筹集的10亿美元资金。

sentences.en: As a result, plans to upgrade the city's century-old subway system are now in doubt.
sentences.zh: 因此，升级这座拥有百年历史的城市地铁系统的计划现在充满了不确定性。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: An audacious raid by the Israeli military over the weekend rescued four Israeli hostages in Gaza who had been held there by Hamas since October 7th and reunited them with their families.
sentences.zh: 以色列军方周末进行了一次孤注一掷的突袭行动，在加沙成功解救了四名自10月7日以来一直被哈马斯扣押的以色列人质，并让他们与家人团聚。

sentences.en: But according to officials in Gaza, the raid killed and wounded scores of Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 但据加沙官员称，此次突袭造成了数十名巴勒斯坦人死伤。

sentences.en: A spokesman for Hamas said that in response, the group would take punitive measures against remaining Israeli hostages in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯发言人表示，作为回应，该组织将对加沙地带剩余的以色列人质采取惩罚性措施。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, a prominent member of Israel's war cabinet, Benny Gantz, quit on Sunday in protest of the government's handling of the war in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，以色列战时内阁的重要成员本尼·甘茨于周日宣布辞职，以抗议政府对加沙战争的处理方式。

sentences.en: Gantz had set this weekend as a deadline for Israel's prime minister to outline a plan to bring the war to an end.
sentences.zh: 甘茨此前曾为以色列总理设定了本周末的最后期限，要求其制定出结束战争的计划。

sentences.en: No such plan has been outlined, prompting Gantz to resign.
sentences.zh: 但并未出台这样的计划，这促使甘茨愤而辞职。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Will Reed, Nina Feldman, Stella Tan, Astha Chantarvedi, and Rochelle Bonja.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由威尔·里德、尼娜·费尔德曼、斯特拉·谭、阿斯塔·钱塔尔维迪和罗谢尔·邦贾制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willens.
sentences.zh: 节目由帕特里夏·威伦斯剪辑。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Alicia Baitu, Dan Powell, and Rowan Amisto, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 包含艾丽西亚·拜图、丹·鲍威尔和罗温·阿米斯特的原创音乐，并由阿丽萨·莫克斯利担任音频工程师。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由仙境乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯伯格创作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运转。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。
